properties.decision:
ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-13, choosing between four options put to him: SPLIT `ifc:mcp-tools` into its stdio and streamable-HTTP transports rather than add `json_rpc` to the `medium` enum.

THE PROBLEM AS IT HAD STOOD SINCE 2026-07-28. `ifc:mcp-tools` claimed `medium: REST`, which was never chosen — it was the schema default before `unspecified` replaced it (`req:seam-incompatibility`), and reflow2's own three boundaries all said REST while being a Rust library API, a document format and an MCP tool surface. The correction was blocked on a genuine vocabulary question and was RAISED FOR HIM RATHER THAN GUESSED, because inventing schema vocabulary is a design decision.

⭐ THE DIAGNOSIS THAT DISSOLVED THE QUESTION: the node's own `endpoint` field already said it — *"a stdio pipe to a launched process, OR the address given to `--http`"*. **One Interface was describing two boundaries.** They differ in more than medium: the HTTP one can be reached remotely, sit behind a gateway and terminate TLS; the stdio one can do none of those, and has no transport to secure at all.

WHAT THE SPLIT COST AND WHAT IT AVOIDED:
  · NO SCHEMA CHANGE, so no new enum value. That matters more than it looks: **enum values are not counted by the version stamp** (it counts node and edge TYPES), so adding one is a compatibility event nothing can detect — the stamp-blindness pattern this design has recorded four instances of already.
  · Existing vocabulary suffices for the half that has an answer: `cli` is exactly right for a launched process spoken to on its stdin/stdout.
  · Four live edges to consider and three `CHANGED` history edges left where they were.

🛑 IT QUARANTINES THE PROBLEM RATHER THAN SOLVING IT, AND THAT WAS SAID BEFORE HE CHOSE. `ifc:mcp-tools-http` still has NO correct enum value and stays `unspecified` rather than taking a wrong one. `medium` is a pairing-key axis where `unspecified` reads as UNKNOWN and never as agreement, **so that boundary cannot pair with anything until the vocabulary question is settled.** Adding `json_rpc` remains open and untaken.

═══ MEASURED IMMEDIATELY AFTER, AND IT VINDICATES THE CUT ═══

`seam_report` against flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api`, run on both halves:

    ifc:mcp-tools-http   agreed 3 · incompatible 1 · unstated 4
                         incompatible: transport_security  ours none / theirs tls
                         unstated:     medium              ours (none) / theirs REST

    ifc:mcp-tools        agreed 3 · incompatible 2 · unstated 3
                         incompatible: medium              ours cli / theirs REST
                         incompatible: transport_security  ours none / theirs tls

⇒ **THE SPLIT MADE THE CHECK ABLE TO TELL THE TWO APART.** The stdio boundary now says loudly, on `medium`, that it is NOT the thing flo2 means — flo2's spec reads *"MCP carried over HTTP, as reflow2 already serves with --http / --serve-shared"*. Before the split a single node would have paired with flo2 ambiguously and carried the TLS finding on the wrong boundary.

📌 AND IT SHARPENS THE OPEN TLS QUESTION. `fact:reflow2-flo2-seam-measured-2026-08-13` recorded two readings of the `transport_security` disagreement: (a) a segment artefact, flo2 terminating TLS at its own edge, or (b) a real assumption gap. On a stdio pipe (a) was arguable, because there is no transport to secure. On the HTTP boundary it is not: that really is plain HTTP with no TLS while flo2 says `tls`. **(b) is now the more likely reading**, and resolving it still needs flo2's side, which was deliberately not written to.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN: whether the `medium` enum should gain `json_rpc` at all. This decision settles only that the surface is two boundaries.
properties.name: The MCP surface is split by transport rather than given a new medium — one Interface was describing two boundaries
properties.rationale:
Recorded as its own accepted Decision rather than by quietly editing the interface, because the interface's spec had carried this as an OPEN question raised for Anthony since 2026-07-28 and the record should show both that it was asked and how it was settled (`dec:reopen-supersedes`' principle).

The load-bearing point is that the question dissolved rather than being answered: the node's own `endpoint` field already described two boundaries, so the missing enum value was a symptom of a modelling error, not a vocabulary gap. Splitting needed no schema change and avoided adding an enum value that the version stamp cannot see.

It is recorded as a partial settlement on purpose. The stdio half now has a correct value (`cli`); the HTTP half has none and stays `unspecified`, which means it cannot pair on medium with anything — including flo2 — until `json_rpc` or an equivalent is decided. That cost was stated before the choice was made rather than discovered afterwards.

Measured the same minute: pairing both halves against flo2 shows the stdio boundary now incompatible on `medium` (correctly — flo2 means the HTTP one) and the HTTP boundary carrying exactly one real disagreement. The split is what let the check tell them apart.
